column7: Discovery took the team several months to complete because we quickly understood that each directorate had a different system and different naming convention. We needed to find a problem to democratize organization-wide data
column8: I ran approximately 75 open-ended interviews (shadowing, doument reviews) with different community leaders, business analysts, and individual users across multiple departments to deeply understand their process and each specific job-to-be-done.
column9: Next, I created a methodology of taking unstructured data and turning it into a structured, quantitative visual matrix for leadership to be able to see overall trends.
column10: Once I understood the key issues, in a second phase of interviews with another 75-80 interviewers, I used a mixture of Figma and Salesforce Lightning to prototype different ideas (low to high fidelity) to understand if I was headed in the right direction. Also, this helped me to communicate these concepts to the dev team
column11: I helped the team understand that what community users wanted was to understand what they needed to do to get their reimbursement as quickly as possible. And that this project of modernizing the software was urgently needed.
column12: The overall project had been on the cusp of being canceled from lack of understanding and my ability to connect the issues to leadership with a simple 88 second upbeat, friendly video, allowed leadership to understand how important this project was to their constituents, and the project was revived.
